name: BloodHound Community Edition
what: A web application that maps relationships in Active Directory and Entra ID as a graph, so you can see attack paths from ordinary users to privileged groups.
when: To find and remove dangerous permission chains (for example a helpdesk group that can reset a Domain Admin's password) before an attacker uses them.
example: Install Docker Desktop on an admin workstation you control.
Download BloodHound CLI from the SpecterOps release page, unpack it and run `bloodhound-cli install`; note the generated admin password.
Sign in at `http://localhost:8080/ui/login` and change the password.
Collect data with the official collectors (SharpHound for AD, AzureHound for Entra ID), upload it, and review paths to Tier 0 groups.
pitfalls: Collectors are often flagged by EDR; agree the run with your security team first.
The collected data is a map for attackers; protect and delete it when done.
Fix paths at their root (group membership, ACLs) rather than removing single edges.
